title: Pan recognition failure
shortDescription: Zone cannot detect a compatible pan.
fullDescription:
Whirlpool induction cooktops show E1 when the active zone does not see ferrous cookware of suitable diameter. The zone times out after about a minute.

Use cookware with the induction symbol on the bottom.

fixSteps.title: Magnet test
fixSteps.instruction: Place a magnet on the pan base.

fixSteps.title: Use bigger pan
fixSteps.instruction: Match pan diameter to the zone marked on the glass.

fixSteps.title: Center pan
fixSteps.instruction: Slide the pan to the center.

faq.a: Smaller than 12 cm rarely couples to the coil.

title: Zone overheated
fullDescription: E2 indicates a thermistor on the coil or IGBT measured a value above the safe ceiling. The cooktop disables the zone until temperatures drop.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Let the cooktop cool for 20 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm cabinet vents are open.

fixSteps.title: Service fan
fixSteps.instruction: If E2 returns at low heat, the fan needs service.

whenToCallPro: Call a tech if the fault returns once the cooktop is cool.

faq.q: Why does my high-heat searing trip E2?
faq.a: Insufficient cabinet airflow lets the inverter overheat.

title: Voltage out of range
fullDescription: E3 indicates the cooktop measured supply voltage outside the safe operating window. Brownouts, lost neutrals, or loose terminals are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Flip breaker off for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Measure supply
fixSteps.instruction: Have an electrician verify L1-L2 is 220-244 V.

fixSteps.title: Repair supply
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten or replace as needed.

whenToCallPro: Always call a licensed electrician for panel work.

faq.a: Only a sine inverter sized for the full load.

title: Touch communication error
shortDescription: UI and main board lost serial link.
fullDescription: E4 indicates the touch board is not communicating with the main control. Loose ribbons, moisture, or a failed UI are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cut breaker for 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cable
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat ribbon between UI and main boards.

fixSteps.title: Replace UI
fixSteps.instruction: If reseating fails, replace UI board.

whenToCallPro: Most owners should call a tech.

title: Coil thermistor open
shortDescription: Coil temperature sensor reads out of range.
fullDescription: E5 indicates the coil thermistor is open or shorted, almost always a wiring or sensor failure. The zone is disabled.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Cut the breaker.

fixSteps.title: Reseat
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the coil thermistor connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the thermistor if reading is bad.

whenToCallPro: Call a tech for inverter access.

faq.q: Can I keep using other zones?
faq.a: Yes if they show no fault.

title: Touch key stuck
shortDescription: A touch key reads as held continuously.
fullDescription: E6 appears when a touch key registers pressure for more than 10 seconds at startup. Cleaning rags or spilled liquids are the usual cause.

fixSteps.title: Wipe dry
fixSteps.instruction: Dry the entire glass.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Flip breaker for 5 minutes.

faq.q: Why does this happen during cleaning?
faq.a: A wet sponge mimics finger pressure.

title: Cooling fan fault
fullDescription: E7 indicates the fan is not running at the expected speed. Dust, a loose plug, or a failed motor are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum vents and fan blades.

fixSteps.title: Reseat plug
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the fan plug.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Replace if fan does not spin.

whenToCallPro: Call if you cannot reach the fan from below.

faq.q: Can I run without the fan?
faq.a: No, the cooktop will continue to throw E2 or E5.

title: EEPROM read error
shortDescription: Control board memory cannot be read.
fullDescription: E8 indicates the main board failed to read its non-volatile memory at startup. A power surge or aging board is usually the cause.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cut breaker for 15 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: If E8 persists, replace the main control board.

whenToCallPro: Most homeowners should call a tech.

faq.a: Yes, after board replacement everything resets to defaults.

title: Inverter over-current
fullDescription: E9 protects the inverter when current spikes. Damaged pans, shorted coils, or failing IGBTs are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Try another pan
fixSteps.instruction: Rule out the cookware.

fixSteps.title: Inspect coil
fixSteps.instruction: Look for soot or burned ferrites.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter
fixSteps.instruction: Replace if IGBT is shorted.

whenToCallPro: E9 is best handled by a qualified tech.

faq.a: Yes if they have separate inverters and show no fault.

title: Control lock active
shortDescription: Control lock has disabled the cooktop.
fullDescription: L indicates the control lock is enabled. Hold the lock key for 3 seconds to disable. If the lock cannot clear, dry the glass and try again.

fixSteps.title: Hold lock key
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the lock key 3 seconds until it chimes.

fixSteps.title: Dry glass
fixSteps.instruction: If unlock fails, wipe the glass dry.

faq.q: Can I disable the lock feature?
faq.a: No, it is a safety feature; only activates by holding the key.
